claims.statement: src/mimetype.rs is the single owner of the project's format vocabulary: lowercase dotless extension constants, a lazily built infer::Infer matcher, and the ARCHIVE_EXTENSIONS / PS3_EXTENSIONS / NON_ORIGINAL_EXTENSIONS groups. It exposes one detection entry point, `pub async fn get_mimetype(path) -> Result<Option<Type>>`, which borrows the shared static MATCHER so one table serves all callers and maps I/O failure to "Failed to infer MIME type"; Ok(None) is a normal "no matcher fired" answer, not an error.

init_matcher() starts from Infer::new() (keeping the crate's built-in zip/7z/gzip detection) and registers ten ROM-specific magic-byte matchers — BPS "BPS1", CHD "MComprHD" (8 bytes), CSO "CISO", IPS "PATCH" (5 bytes), IRD "3IRD", RDSK "RDSK", RIFF "RIFF", RVZ "RVZ"+0x01, XDELTA D6 C3 C4 (3 bytes) and ZSO with the magic "ZISO" — each as a pure &[u8] -> bool that checks buf.len() before indexing so truncated headers return false instead of panicking. RVZ pins the version byte to 0x01, so a future RVZ revision is not detected by content.

Because each matcher is registered with an extension constant, `Type::extension()` returns exactly that constant, which is why callers across the codebase compare mimetype.extension() against CHD_EXTENSION, ARCHIVE_EXTENSIONS and PatchType/XsoType strum variants; roughly twenty modules import the whole module with `use super::mimetype::*;`.

import_rom() resolves a single extension string for dispatch: it calls get_mimetype and uses mimetype.extension() when a matcher fired, otherwise falls back to path.extension() lowercased; that string then selects the archive / CHD / CIA / CSO / NSZ / RVZ / ZSO / import_other cascade, and every non-default branch is additionally gated on !as_is so --as-is sends any container straight to import_other. import_roms::main reuses the same detection to order parent-declaring CHDs before their parents (the priority coming from parse_chd's parent sha1, not the file name) and to unpack top-level archives under --extract.

In contrast to import, conversion/export partitioning never inspects file bytes: partition_games_by_extensions and partition_games_by_all_extensions split games by testing romfile.path.ends_with(extension) against the stored romfiles.path string, and check_roms dispatches on the resolved path's extension. The resulting invariant is that once a file is in the database its recorded extension, not its content, selects the pipeline — a CHD renamed .iso is converted as an ISO.

ARCHIVE_EXTENSIONS (7z, zip) is the predicate for treating a romfile as a multi-entry container: import_roms unpacks and matches entries individually (also under --extract, via the mimetype extension), rebuild_roms extracts an existing archive before re-importing, check_roms routes to check_archive, and CommonRomfile::get_sorted_path suppresses the per-game arcade subfolder when the extension is an archive.

NON_ORIGINAL_EXTENSIONS (chd, cso, nsz, rvz, zso, 7z, zip) defines which ROM entries are recompressions rather than catalog originals: import_dats stores original = !NON_ORIGINAL_EXTENSIONS.contains(ext), convert-roms loads its candidates through load_rom_data(..., true) which filters on original = true (export-roms passes false and takes all), and get_sorted_path names a non-original file after the game instead of the DAT rom name. Removing a format from this list would make conversion treat its containers as originals.

PS3_EXTENSIONS (pkg, pup, rap) changes how a single-file archive is placed on import: when the matched DAT rom's extension is one of these (or the system is arcade), the extracted file is renamed {game.name}.{archive extension} rather than the rom's own name with the archive extension swapped in.

Format-entry guards validate inconsistently, and the difference is externally visible: as_chd, as_riff, as_rdsk and as_xso call get_mimetype and bail when nothing matches (as_chd then parses the container, and as_xso derives XsoType from the mimetype extension, so cso and zso share one romfile type), while as_iso, as_cue_bin, as_rvz, as_nsz and as_nsp only compare path.extension() lowercased against their constant and AsArchive::as_archive maps it through ArchiveType::from_str. RVZ consequently has a magic matcher its own guard never consults, and NSZ/NSP are typed by name alone.

Patches rely on content with no filename fallback: parse_patch maps PatchType::from_str(mimetype.extension()) and a file no matcher recognizes is reported as "Unsupported patch format". parse_ird likewise requires a mimetype and uses it to choose the reader — gz triggers a GzDecoder wrapper, ird reads raw, anything else bails "Not an IRD file" — which only works because infer's built-in gzip matcher shares the same MATCHER table.

Where the stored extension is insufficient, convert_roms re-queries the mimetype locally: after extracting a single archive entry it overrides the extracted extension with the detected one unless it is iso, then matches iso/rdsk/riff to select CD/HD/LD CHD compression settings; the leftover `others` partition (not archive, CUE/BIN, ISO, CSO, ZSO or CHD) is typed purely by get_mimetype for the same reason, and an unrecognized type prints "Unsupported file type, skipping" instead of aborting the run.

Adding a format requires coordinated mimetype.rs edits that the compiler cannot enforce: add the lowercase extension constant, add a length-checked matcher plus a matcher.add registration when magic bytes exist, and update the extension groups downstream dispatch reads (NON_ORIGINAL_EXTENSIONS for recompressions, ARCHIVE_EXTENSIONS for multi-entry containers — which also changes arcade folder placement), then wire import_rom dispatch, check_roms and the partition_games_by_extensions splits in convert_roms/export_roms, which match path string suffixes rather than parsed extensions.

Detection is unit-tested per matcher: src/mimetype/test_bps_matcher.rs through test_zso_matcher.rs each assert test_valid (exact magic), test_invalid (right length, wrong bytes) and test_too_short (magic minus one byte), covering the length guard rather than path handling; get_mimetype itself has no direct test and is exercised indirectly by the per-format import tests over fixtures in tests/.

A CHD's actual type is resolved by parsing the container with chd-rs, not by mimetype sniffing: AsChd::parse_chd opens the file on the blocking pool and returns ChdType (Cd/Dvd/Ld mapped from chd_rs::ChdType, everything else Hd), logical size, data SHA-1, file SHA-1, optional parent SHA-1 and CD track count, so hashes and size come from the header instead of a read pass — and a CD deliberately reports size 0 with an empty data SHA-1 because only its tracks have those. CHD support is entirely in-process: chd::get_version() returns the literal "built-in", and no code path resolves a chdman binary.

Each ChdType round-trips through its own neutral payload, which is why the rdsk and riff matchers exist: ToIso/ToRdsk/ToRiff/ToCueBin extract a DVD/HD/LD/CD CHD to .iso/.rdsk/.riff/(CUE+BIN) and each re-validates the result through as_iso/as_rdsk/as_riff, so an LD CHD passes through RIFF on the way out and back in. transcode::romfile_as_chd is the single entry point that chooses parent handling — as_chd_with_parent when the database records a parent_id, plain as_chd (which scans the containing directory for a sibling CHD whose file SHA-1 equals the header's parent_sha1) otherwise — and check_roms, convert_roms and export_roms all obtain ChdRomfiles through it.

rdsk and riff are reachable only through content detection: outside src/chd.rs the RDSK_EXTENSION and RIFF_EXTENSION constants appear solely in convert_roms' to_chd paths — the archive-entry override (extracted extension replaced by the detected one unless it is iso) and the leftover `others` partition typed entirely by get_mimetype — so no import, check or export branch dispatches on them and unmatched files print "Unsupported file type, skipping".

check_roms is the least forgiving dispatcher: it selects the archive/CHD/CSO/NSZ/RVZ/ZSO/plain branch from romfile_path.extension() without lowercasing, so an upper-case extension falls through to the plain check, and because the CHD, CSO, ZSO, NSZ and RVZ branches call their guards with `?`, a container that fails to open or whose bytes are not CISO/ZISO aborts check_system entirely instead of counting one error and moving the file to Trash — only failures returned from a completed check() take the report-and-trash path.

MAME-style DAT entries make a CHD non-original by having no extension at all: import_dats computes original with PathBuf::from(name).extension().is_some_and(|ext| !NON_ORIGINAL_EXTENSIONS.contains(ext)), so a <disk name="game"> entry (no dot in the name) yields original = false just as a "game.chd" rom entry does, and those roms are consequently excluded from convert-roms' load_rom_data(..., true) candidate set.

The LaserDisc and arcade-HD CHD paths are covered by dedicated fixtures rather than an LD import test: tests/Test Game (USA, Europe) (LD).riff drives src/chd/test_ld.rs, which asserts a RIFF to CHD to RIFF to CHD cycle yields a byte-identical second CHD and that the parsed container reports ChdType::Ld with non-zero size, while tests/Test Game (USA, Europe) (RDSK).chd drives import_roms' MAME CHD tests, which place the file at {system}/{game}/{rom}.chd under an arcade system.
